entries.effect: the class is declared and exported, so NSClassFromString answers for it: -PDFDataWithActions: draws the block into a PDF context CoreGraphics makes from the format's bounds - a page of US Letter when those are empty - and answers a copy of the bytes, or an empty NSData rather than nil when there was no context to draw into and the block did not run; -writePDFToURL:withActions:error: draws the same document into the file the URL names. What lands in the file is the release's own PDF writer, not a re-implementation of one

entries.reason: the blocks run through UIView's own animation and, for an interruptible animator, are paused and scrubbed from there, which is what UIKit does; only the animations this animator added are held, by layer and key, so nothing else on those layers is stopped

entries.reason: the release's own -setItems: does the storing; the two 10.0 options are read and applied by nothing
entries.effect: the items are handed to the release's own -setItems:, so a caller reads back whatever the release kept, and the two options are READ and recorded against the pasteboard and applied by nothing: this release has no pasteboard option keys, no store that syncs between devices and no item expiry. What the release does with the items is its own answer and not measured here - facts/UIKit/UIPasteboardIOS10.md measures a write on an emulated iOS 6.0 being taken and silently lost, with -setStrings: the one that raises
entries.source: objc.inventory on the 6.1.3 and 4.3 caches, negative controls included, says the release ships UIPasteboard, and the release's selector table holds -setItems:, so this is a category over the system's class

entries.reason: UITextView on this release carries no TextKit surface at all (measured on the iPad 2, 6.1.3: no textContainer/layoutManager/textStorage selector; its ivars are entirely WebKit's own, m_webView/UIWebDocumentView, m_body/DOMHTMLElement, m_frame/WebFrame), so there is no NSTextContainer for this property to describe
entries.effect: the value round-trips exactly (kept, handed back unmodified) and is applied as the WebKit document body's CSS padding, confirmed on the iPad 2 by reading DOMCSSStyleDeclaration.padding back after setting the property; nothing that presumes a real text container (glyph-level measurement, container size) is added
entries.source: the iPad 2, 6.1.3: UITextView's ivars (class introspection) and a live app run confirming the round trip and the DOM padding it produces
